note: Plain-text knot steps for the Learn page. 'picture' and 'credit' are left empty on purpose: a licensed diagram and its credit line go there later.

knots.name: Palomar
knots.what: A very strong, simple knot for tying line to a hook, lure or swivel. It works well with braided line.
knots.use: Your everyday knot for hooks, jigs and swivels, especially with braid.
steps: Double about 6 inches of line and pass the loop through the eye of the hook.
Tie a loose overhand knot with the doubled line (the hook hangs from the loop).
Pull the loop of line down over the whole hook, past the eye.
Wet the knot with water, then pull the standing line and the tail slowly to tighten.
Trim the tail close.
knots.tip: The hook must be small enough for the loop to pass over it. For a large lure, use another knot.

knots.name: Improved clinch
knots.what: A classic knot for tying line to a hook, lure or swivel.
knots.use: Mono or fluorocarbon line to hooks and lures. Less reliable in slick braid.
steps: Pass the line through the eye and pull about 6 inches through.
Wrap the tail around the standing line 5 to 7 times.
Pass the tail through the small loop next to the eye.
Pass the tail back through the big loop that just formed.
Wet the knot and pull the standing line to tighten, then trim.
knots.tip: Use fewer wraps (about 5) on thick line and more (up to 7) on thin line.

knots.name: Uni
knots.what: A versatile knot that ties line to a hook, or one line to another when used twice.
knots.use: Hooks, swivels and lures with any kind of line, including braid.
steps: Pass the line through the eye and double back 6 inches, so the tail lies along the standing line.
Make a loop with the tail that passes back beside the eye.
Wrap the tail around both lines and through the loop 4 to 6 times.
Wet the knot and pull the tail to snug the wraps.
Slide the knot down to the eye by pulling the standing line, then trim.
knots.tip: Leave it loose and slide it to the eye if you want a small loop for lure action.

knots.name: Loop knot
knots.what: A knot that leaves a small open loop so a lure can swing freely.
knots.use: Lures that work better with free movement, like jerkbaits, topwater plugs and flies.
steps: Tie a loose overhand knot in the line, about 6 inches from the end.
Pass the tail through the lure's eye, then back through the overhand knot in the same direction.
Wrap the tail around the standing line 3 to 5 times.
Pass the tail back through the overhand knot, the same way it entered.
Wet the knot, pull on the tail and standing line to tighten, then trim, leaving the loop the size you want.
knots.tip: Check the loop size before you pull tight; a smaller loop gives more control, a larger one more swing.

knots.name: Albright
knots.what: A knot that joins two lines of different thickness, such as braid to a mono or fluorocarbon leader.
knots.use: Joining a leader to your main line.
steps: Make a loop in the thicker line (the leader) and pass about 8 inches of the thin line (braid) through it.
Hold the loop and both tails, then wrap the thin line back over itself and the loop 10 to 12 times, working toward the loop end.
Pass the end of the thin line back through the loop, exiting on the same side it entered.
Wet it and pull both ends of the thin line slowly to tighten the wraps.
Pull the main line and the leader to seat the knot, then trim the tails.
knots.tip: Take your time tightening: neat, snug wraps matter more than speed.

knots.name: Double uni
knots.what: Two uni knots tied around each other to join two lines.
knots.use: Joining main line to a leader, or tying new line onto old.
steps: Overlap the two line ends by about 8 inches, side by side.
With one tail, tie a uni knot around the other line, with 4 to 6 wraps, and tighten it slightly.
Do the same with the other tail around the first line.
Wet both knots and pull the two standing lines in opposite directions so the knots slide together.
Trim both tails.
knots.tip: Use fewer wraps on thick leader and more wraps on thin braid.

knots.name: Nail knot
knots.what: A slim knot that joins a leader to the main line and passes smoothly through rod guides.
knots.use: Fly line to leader or backing, or a leader to braid for a smooth join.
steps: Lay a small tube (a thin straw or tube works) or a nail along the main line, with the leader on the other side, pointing the opposite way.
Wrap the leader tail around the main line and the tube 5 to 7 times.
Pass the end of the leader back through the tube.
Hold the wraps and pull the tube out, then wet and pull the leader slowly to tighten.
Trim the tails.
knots.tip: A slim tube makes this much easier to learn than a nail.

knots.name: Blood knot
knots.what: A neat, smooth way to join two lines of nearly the same thickness.
knots.use: Joining two pieces of mono or fluorocarbon.
steps: Overlap the two ends by about 6 inches.
Wrap one tail around the other line 5 times, then bring it back between the two lines.
Wrap the other tail around the first line 5 times in the opposite direction, and bring it back between the lines through the same gap, going the opposite way.
Wet the knot and pull both standing lines slowly so the wraps close together.
Trim both tails.
knots.tip: The knot is best with lines of similar thickness; for different thicknesses use an Albright or double uni.
